text:
maria: kicking off canary for model v12 -> 10% traffic. want to enable automatic fallbacks so user requests stay live if the canary misbehaves :grimacing:

dan: can you summarize what fallbacks you want? there are a few layers (model variant, region, capacity).

maria: yeah — plan is: primary = v12 quantized, fallback1 = v11 (same region), fallback2 = v11 in another region, final = smaller cheap model (v10-lite). also want a fast failover if latency spike > 2s P95 for 2 consecutive minutes.

jyoti: +1 for multilevel. question: do we let traffic continue to route to canary while fallbacks are active, or pause canary until we fix it?

maria: prefer graceful degradation — let canary keep some traffic but circuit-break if error rate > 5% for 3m. otherwise fallback per-request.

eli: op note: per-request fallback has perf implications (extra routing hops). we should avoid synchronous retries to different regions unless we do hedged reads.

kai: propose policy DSL like below for rollout config. small and explicit so UI can show it:

```yaml
rollout:
  id: v12-canary-2026-03
  traffic_split: 10
  fallbacks:
    - type: model_variant
      selector: v11
      max_extra_latency_ms: 200
    - type: regional
      selector: us-west-2:v11
      max_extra_latency_ms: 400
    - type: cost-saving
      selector: v10-lite
      max_extra_latency_ms: 800
  circuit_breakers:
    latency_p95_ms: 2000
    error_rate_pct: 5
    window_minutes: 3
```

dan: looks good. couple of UX asks: console should show which fallback served each request (so customers can see quality impact) and provide toggle to disable regional fallback for compliance reasons.

maria: yup, add `expose_fallback_reason: true` and `allowed_fallbacks` whitelist per-tenant.

jyoti: how do we detect when to promote/demote canary? metric-based or manual?

maria: started with metric-based: if canary error_rate < 1% and latency delta < 10% for 30m -> promote. otherwise auto-rollback on circuit break. manual override still allowed.

eli: implementation detail: runtime should do a single decision per-request: resolve fallback chain, then route. avoid doing extra probe requests. caching the last-good-route per-user for short TTL helps.

kai: also consider quota interactions: if fallback goes to cheap model but tenant is on a particular quota for that model, we mustn't violate SLAs. add check: `quota_aware: true` in the DSL.

maria: ok add that. one more: telemetry — we need structured tags: rollout_id, fallback_step, reason, decision_time, latency_ms. will feed into console and alerts.

deploy-bot: deploy started for v12-canary-2026-03 at 2026-03-18T15:08:43Z :rocket:

dan: timeline: can we get a quick POC in staging today? small PR to runtime + UI flags. I can take the runtime piece. jyoti can do console vis.

jyoti: on it. will mock the `fallback_reason` column and add a tooltip explaining steps.

eli: I'll add hedging toggle: `enable_region_hedging: true|false`. default false to avoid cross-region costs.

kai: test cases we need:
- canary with transient latency spike (should fallback per-request, then resume)
- sustained error rate (should circuit-break and stop sending new canary traffic)
- regional outage (should route to allowed region or cost-saving model)
- tenant with regional restrictions (should never use regional fallback)

maria: perfect. one more operational thought: clear logs when fallback happens and push alert rule if fallback_rate > 2% for 5m. we don't want silent degradation.

dan: agree. also need an audit trail showing who changed allowed_fallbacks list.

maria: ok i'll draft the RFC with the DSL, telemetry schema, and rollout guardrails. aim to ship POC by EOD. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

kai: small nit — call the final cheap model `graceful_fallback` in the UI to avoid customers thinking it's a permanent downgrade.

maria: good call. adding that to docs.

deploy-bot: deploy completed for v12-canary-2026-03 in staging :white_check_mark:
